notes: Primary ask: replace current homegrown scoring service with LLM-based reranker for RTB pipeline — hard p99/throughput SLOs.
Current infra: multi-region AWS (us-east-1 primary) with VPC-only endpoints for inference. Prefer dedicated capacity but open to hybrid.
Key constraints: end-to-end latency budget for scoring stage is 25-40ms (including network). Cost sensitivity: wants <= $0.006 per 1k tokens equivalent across high-volume flows.
EdgeForm engineering quote: 'We need deterministic tail behavior — batching and KV cache can't increase our p99 beyond 10ms budget for reranker.'
SE note: recommend Redwood Optimize recommendations + dedicated pool with sub-ms local batching and prefix caching for identical auction contexts.

requirements_summary: Workload: high-volume, short-context reranking and feature-embedding calls per auction (avg tokens 40-120).
Targets: p50 < 8ms, p95 < 18ms, p99 < 35ms for reranker at 2k qps sustained; burst to 8k qps tolerable with graceful degradation.
Cost: target unit economics aligned to current shim at ~ $0.005 per 1k token-equivalent. Prioritize batching/caching/quantization to hit that target.
Model preferences: open Llama-like family for on-prem compatibility; want option to route to smaller quantized variants during spikes.
Routing/fallback: require automated fallback to quantized/cheaper model tier and cross-region failover.
perf_targets: Sustained throughput: 2,000 QPS for reranking workload
Burst handling: maintain p95 degradation <= 2x baseline during 5m bursts up to 8,000 QPS
test_plan: Traffic replay using 7 days of production auctions (anonymized) — run full P99 curves
A/B canary: 10% traffic to Redwood Dedicated pool for 2 weeks, compare latency and cost per request
Quantization experiment: int8 vs int4 on equivalent models; evaluate quality delta on held-out eval set
Batching matrix: evaluate 1..16 concurrency and autoregressive batching impact on tail latencies
KV caching: run prefix cache for repeated user-profile prefixes; measure token savings and latency impact
recent_poc_results: Initial POC (2026-02-10): microbench with small sample — batching=4 reduced per-token compute by ~38% but added 3-6ms to tail in current config
Quantization (int8) trial: model size down 2.7x, latency improved in median but some p95 regressions on long contexts; need tuned kernels
Cache test: identical-auction prefix cache yielded 22% token hit rate during prime hours; when combined with batching, net cost down ~30%
Open items: kernel-level optimizations for int4, network topology for sub-10ms p99 remains unresolved
